thesis.thesis_text: Vallibel Power Erathna PLC is a hydropower generator (Erathna, Kiriwaneliya and Denawaka Ganga mini-hydro plants) that has just brought a new Dolahena Estate ground-mounted solar plant online. Group revenue grew 26.2% YoY to Rs.535.4mn in Q1 FY2026/27, almost entirely because Dolahena generated 4,653k MWh and Rs.118.6mn of revenue versus nil a year earlier -- the existing hydro fleet was flat to down, with Erathna MHP generation falling 11.2% YoY. Group PAT still grew 12.4% to Rs.301.3mn despite finance costs surging from Rs.1.0mn to Rs.36.4mn as the Rs.1.37bn of debt drawn to fund Dolahena began accruing a full quarter's interest. At a 10.6x run-rate P/E but 3.0x P/B, the stock is not statistically cheap on book, and the FY2026 DPS of Rs.0.60 continues a declining trend from Rs.1.75 in FY2024, likely reflecting capital retention for the solar buildout (Q1 FY2026/27 filing, source_doc_id manual_721c870d72fd674c).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/weather/regulatory-tariff data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter of financial_statements is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period P&L/balance-sheet trend), though a 6-year dividend history (FY2021-FY2026) partially offsets this; no rainfall/hydrology commentary is disclosed by the company to explain the Erathna plant's generation decline.

financial_quality.rationale: Group operating margin remained high at 73.6% this quarter (2025: 77.0%) and net margin 56.3% (2025: 63.2%) -- typical for a hydropower generator with low variable costs. Current ratio (current assets Rs.1,706.4mn / current liabilities Rs.362.2mn) of ~4.7x indicates strong short-term liquidity. Finance costs surged from Rs.1.0mn to Rs.36.4mn (>999% per the filing's own variance column) as Rs.1,372.0mn of combined interest-bearing borrowings, drawn to fund the new Dolahena solar plant, began accruing a full quarter's interest -- a meaningful step-change in leverage (borrowings vs Rs.3,799.7mn total equity, D/E ~0.36) that should be monitored but is not yet a red flag given PAT still grew.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group revenue +26.2% YoY to Rs.535.4mn and PAT +12.4% to Rs.301.3mn, driven almost entirely by the new Dolahena Estate solar plant (4,653k MWh, Rs.118.6mn revenue vs nil a year earlier) -- a genuine new capacity addition, not a one-off item, so this growth should recur going forward. However, the existing hydro fleet was flat to down, with Erathna MHP generation falling 11.2% YoY (15,004k to 13,328k thousand MWh) with no rainfall/hydrology commentary given -- ex-Dolahena, generation from the three hydro plants actually declined, so growth is concentrated in one new asset rather than broad-based.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.15.30 (2026-08-28), annualising Q1 FY2026/27 Group basic EPS of Rs.0.36 (x4 = Rs.1.44) implies a run-rate P/E of ~10.6x -- reasonable for a regulated utility. Total equity of Rs.3,799,749,849 / 747,109,731 shares implies NAV/share of ~Rs.5.09, so P/B is a richer ~3.0x. FY2026 DPS of Rs.0.60 (yield ~3.9%) continues a declining trend from Rs.1.75 (FY2024) and Rs.0.75 (FY2025), likely reflecting capital retention for the Dolahena capex cycle rather than distress, but it tempers the valuation picture versus a simple cheap-P/E read.
citations: dividends: FY2026 DPS 0.60, FY2025 DPS 0.75, FY2024 DPS 1.75

business_quality.rationale: Established regulated power generator (Utilities sector) with three mini-hydro plants (Erathna, Kiriwaneliya, Denawaka Ganga) now diversifying into solar (Dolahena), which should reduce single-technology hydrology risk over time. The Group's only disclosed contingent liability (Rs.651.7mn customs bank guarantee for solar-panel imports) is an import/customs exposure, not FX-denominated debt, and no foreign-currency borrowings are disclosed -- a cleaner risk profile than an FX-exposed exporter. Erathna's 11.2% generation decline this quarter is the main quality concern.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists to independently verify board or ownership changes. Disclosure quality in this filing is otherwise good: the Company transparently flagged a post-period-end Rs.430.0mn dividend received from its subsidiary (Note 10) and clearly itemised its one material contingent liability. No red flags found, but no independent governance data source exists to go further.

key_reasons: Group PAT +12.4% YoY to Rs.301.3mn on 26.2% revenue growth, with the new Dolahena solar plant (4,653k MWh, Rs.118.6mn revenue vs nil a year ago) now fully operational and driving essentially all of the growth

Group operating margin remains high (73.6% this quarter) and current ratio of ~4.7x indicates strong short-term liquidity, though finance costs rose >999% YoY as Rs.1.37bn of Dolahena project debt began accruing a full quarter's interest

P/E of ~10.6x (run-rate) looks reasonable but P/B of ~3.0x is not cheap, and DPS has declined from Rs.1.75 (FY2024) to Rs.0.60 (FY2026), consistent with capital being retained for the solar expansion rather than distributed
watch_factors: Erathna MHP generation fell 11.2% YoY (15,004k to 13,328k thousand MWh) with no rainfall/hydrology commentary disclosed -- worth monitoring whether this is a one-quarter dip or a longer decline at that plant

Finance costs on the Dolahena-related debt (Rs.1.37bn combined borrowings) will run at a full annualised rate going forward (versus a partial quarter this period) -- next quarter's PBT growth could look weaker on a like-for-like basis even if generation holds

DPS fell from Rs.1.75 (FY2024) to Rs.0.75 (FY2025) to Rs.0.60 (FY2026) -- a declining trend that could reverse once the Dolahena capex cycle completes, or could signal a structurally lower payout going forward

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 will show whether Dolahena's revenue run-rate holds and whether Erathna's generation recovers from this quarter's 11.2% YoY decline.
horizon_notes.1y: A full year of Dolahena's contribution plus a full year of its associated finance costs will clarify the plant's true incremental earnings contribution and whether DPS growth resumes.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether the diversification into solar reduces VPEL's hydrology-driven earnings volatility over a multi-year horizon without eroding returns via higher leverage.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/rate-cycle or long-term rainfall/climate data source in this project to assess multi-year hydrology or tariff-regime risk for VPEL's generation mix.

interim_updates.note_text: Vallibel Power Erathna PLC (VPEL) reported Group revenue of Rs.535.4mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 26.2% YoY from Rs.424.1mn, and Group PAT rose 12.4% YoY to Rs.301.3mn (from Rs.268.0mn). The plant-level segment note (pp.6-7) shows the revenue growth was driven almost entirely by the new Dolahena Estate Ground-Mounted Solar PV Project (GMSP), which generated 4,653 thousand MWh and Rs.118.6mn of revenue this quarter versus nil a year earlier (the project was still under construction in Q1 FY2025/26, when Rs.753.6mn of Group capex went into 'Acquisitions of Property, Plant & Equipment' per the cash flow statement, versus just Rs.26.1mn this quarter now that the plant is operational). Excluding Dolahena, the three hydro plants' combined generation was essentially flat to down: Erathna MHP generation fell 11.2% YoY (15,004k to 13,328k thousand MWh, revenue down 8.5% to Rs.111.3mn), consistent with weaker inflows at that plant this quarter (no explicit rainfall/hydrology commentary is given by the company); Kiriwaneliya MHP generation was roughly flat (+0.2%, 7,710k to 7,726k thousand MWh); Denawaka Ganga MHP generation rose 5.3% (4,040k to 4,254k thousand MWh). Group gross profit rose a smaller 20.5% YoY to Rs.454.5mn (from Rs.377.3mn) as direct costs rose faster than revenue (+72.8% YoY to Rs.80.9mn, from Rs.46.8mn, reflecting the new Dolahena plant's own operating costs). Below gross profit, finance cost surged from just Rs.1.0mn to Rs.36.4mn (the filing's own variance column shows '>999%') as the debt drawn to fund the Dolahena project -- Rs.1,176.0mn non-current plus Rs.196.0mn current interest-bearing borrowings outstanding at 30 June 2026 -- began accruing a full quarter's interest now that the project is complete (versus Rs.418.1mn of NEW borrowings drawn but not yet fully interest-bearing for a full quarter in the prior-year comparative). PBT still grew 11.5% YoY to Rs.374.5mn (from Rs.335.8mn) because the Dolahena revenue contribution outweighed the finance-cost increase; PAT grew a smaller 12.4% (similar rate, tax expense +8.0% YoY was proportionate). At the Company (parent-only, non-consolidated) level, revenue rose 88.9% YoY to Rs.229.8mn and PAT rose 44.9% YoY to Rs.80.7mn. No FX-denominated borrowing is disclosed -- the Group's only contingent liability is a Rs.651.7mn bank guarantee to Sri Lanka Customs for the Dolahena solar-panel import Bonding Warehouse facility (Note 6, p.7), a customs/import exposure rather than an FX-debt exposure.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for VPEL in this database, so no prior quarter (Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column (three months ended 30 June 2025) is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) VPEL's P&L format has no explicit 'Operating Profit' line -- operating_profit in financial_statements is a derived figure (Gross Profit - Admin Expenses - Other Operating Expenses), not a number VPEL itself discloses; (2) no explicit rainfall/hydrology commentary is given anywhere in the filing to explain why Erathna MHP generation fell 11.2% YoY -- this is inferred from the segment table's own generation-volume figures, not company commentary, and could reflect lower inflows, planned maintenance, or another cause not disclosed; (3) no plant-level average tariff or PPA (power purchase agreement) rate is disclosed, so it is not possible to separate volume effects from price effects within each segment's revenue change; (4) no explicit statement confirms whether the Dolahena project's interest-bearing borrowings are LKR-denominated or carry any foreign-currency component -- the only currency-relevant disclosure is the customs bank guarantee (Rs.651.7mn, LKR) for imported solar equipment, which is an import/customs exposure rather than a financing FX exposure.
interim_updates.takeaway: Group revenue grew 26.2% YoY to Rs.535.4mn almost entirely because the new Dolahena Ground-Mounted Solar PV Project became operational this quarter, generating 4,653 thousand MWh and Rs.118.6mn of revenue versus nil a year earlier -- the existing hydro fleet was flat to slightly down (Erathna MHP generation -11.2% YoY was the one notable soft spot). PAT still grew a healthy 12.4% to Rs.301.3mn despite finance cost surging from Rs.1.0mn to Rs.36.4mn as the Dolahena project's debt (Rs.1.37bn combined current+non-current borrowings) began accruing a full quarter's interest -- the new plant's revenue contribution more than absorbed the higher financing cost.
operational_highlights: Group revenue up 26.2% YoY to Rs.535.4mn (from Rs.424.1mn); Group PAT up 12.4% YoY to Rs.301.3mn (from Rs.268.0mn); EPS Rs.0.36 (from Rs.0.32)

Dolahena Estate Ground-Mounted Solar PV Project (GMSP) generated 4,653 thousand MWh and Rs.118.6mn revenue this quarter, versus nil a year earlier (segment note, pp.6-7) -- the single largest driver of Group revenue growth, now that the plant is operational after Rs.753.6mn of construction-phase capex a year ago

Erathna MHP generation fell 11.2% YoY (15,004k to 13,328k thousand MWh), revenue down 8.5% to Rs.111.3mn -- the one plant showing a genuine year-on-year decline; Kiriwaneliya MHP roughly flat (+0.2%); Denawaka Ganga MHP up 5.3%

Group direct costs rose 72.8% YoY to Rs.80.9mn (from Rs.46.8mn), faster than revenue growth, reflecting the new Dolahena plant's own operating cost base -- gross profit grew a smaller 20.5% YoY to Rs.454.5mn

Finance cost surged from Rs.1.0mn to Rs.36.4mn (filing's own variance column: '>999%') as Rs.1,372.0mn of combined interest-bearing borrowings (drawn to fund Dolahena) began accruing a full quarter's interest now the project is complete
Group capex (PPE acquisitions) fell to Rs.26.1mn from Rs.753.6mn a year earlier -- confirms the Dolahena construction phase is substantially complete
Company (parent-only) revenue up 88.9% YoY to Rs.229.8mn, PAT up 44.9% YoY to Rs.80.7mn

Contingent liability: Rs.651.7mn in bank guarantees to Sri Lanka Customs for the Dolahena solar-panel import Bonding Warehouse facility (Note 6, p.7) -- an import/customs exposure, not FX-denominated debt; no foreign-currency borrowings disclosed
Post-period event: Company received a Rs.430.0mn net dividend from subsidiary Country Energy (Pvt) Ltd on 13 July 2026 (Note 10, p.8), not reflected in these 30 June 2026 figures
key_drivers: Dolahena GMSP (solar) contributed Rs.118.6mn revenue and 4,653 thousand MWh of generation this quarter versus nil a year earlier (segment note, pp.6-7) -- the single largest driver of the 26.2% Group revenue growth

Finance cost rose from Rs.1,006,514 to Rs.36,376,394 (>999% per the filing's own variance column) as the Dolahena project's debt began accruing a full quarter's interest -- the main drag between the 20.5% gross-profit growth and the smaller 11.5% PBT growth

Erathna MHP generation -11.2% YoY (15,004k to 13,328k thousand MWh, segment note) -- the one existing plant with a clear year-on-year decline, consistent with weaker hydrology at that site though not explicitly attributed to rainfall by the company

Direct costs +72.8% YoY (Rs.46,829,497 to Rs.80,893,571), outpacing revenue growth and reflecting the new Dolahena plant's operating cost base -- the reason gross-profit growth (20.5%) trailed revenue growth (26.2%)
